primary_antecedent.scope: Antecedent for solution/parametrix comparison. The actual weak local matrix matching and finite-order receiving checks are independently proved here.

source_correspondence: The receiving problem is the actual normalized real scalar-principal matrix equation at a strict diffractive point. It needs no physical time function and permits tangentially regular sources rough in the normal direction.
The boundary mixed eikonal identity makes theta_q zero; the fixed-depth Airy derivatives dominate its O(q lambda) correction and identify the signs of both ordinary branches.

The full unnormalized mode has smooth PDE error on the attained interior slab directly from CAA residual coefficients. No exponentially growing inverse multiplier is applied to a normalized smoothing error.
The negative Cauchy row is an elliptic order-five-sixths graph operator. Its proper inverse includes every lower matrix and normal amplitude term.
The actual weak Cauchy trace has order minus one-half before inversion. The first compact coefficient has order one-third and matches that trace modulo a full smooth kernel.
The exact residual evolution retains source, extension, factorization and cutoff errors. All-real weak uniqueness and negative-root ellipticity give incoming matching.
A bounded interior extractor upgrades the coefficient to H5/6 without assuming a represented energy field. The stable coefficient is twice the unnormalized incoming coefficient.
The actual boundary inverse, layer-trace estimate and bounded ordinary localization construct the second compact precursor in H_L.

The normalized kernel exists as a finite-order normal distribution before an energy estimate for that input. Its exact positive-branch identity proves incoming regularity without a physical-wave assumption.
Every finite-order Dirichlet comparison hypothesis is checked for the actual residual. Its one fixed accessible region gives all tangential mixed orders and actual smooth boundary traces.
The full stable coefficient norm remains unproved for these localized data. The local extracted oscillating coefficient is distinguished from the global weighted term and its input displacement.
The three solutions verify Cauchy signs and the factor two, separate the two weighted spaces, and exhibit normal roughness compatible with the source hypotheses.
The 92 external human foundations are retained as external. All nine admitted books remain valid.
